text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines information retrieval with text generation. A retriever selects relevant documents, which are passed to a language model as context.
Precision at k measures the fraction of the top k retrieved results that are relevant to a query.
Recall at k measures the fraction of all known relevant documents that appear in the top k retrieved results.
Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) measures how highly the first relevant result appears in a ranked list of search results.
A regression test checks whether a change to software causes previously working behavior to fail.
A vector embedding represents text as a numerical vector. Semantically similar text can have vectors that are close together in the embedding space.
Chunking divides a long document into smaller passages before indexing. Chunk size and overlap can affect retrieval quality and the amount of context available.
Hybrid search combines lexical retrieval, such as BM25, with dense vector retrieval to capture both exact term matches and semantic similarity.
A reranker takes an initial set of retrieved candidates and scores them again to improve their ordering for a particular query.
Grounded generation means producing an answer supported by the supplied evidence. Citation checks can verify whether cited source documents actually support the answer.
A prompt injection attack attempts to manipulate an AI system using instructions embedded in user input or retrieved content. Retrieved documents should be treated as untrusted data.
A retrieval benchmark should contain representative questions, expected relevant documents, and documented evaluation criteria. Test data should be kept separate from development data.
Precision at k is the number of relevant documents among the top k results divided by k, when k retrieved results are available.
Recall at k is the number of relevant documents retrieved in the top k divided by the total number of known relevant documents for the query.
Mean Reciprocal Rank averages the reciprocal rank of the first relevant result across a set of queries. A higher value rewards relevant results appearing earlier.
Latency measures the time taken for an operation to complete. Percentile latency, including p95, helps describe slower requests rather than only the average.
Caching stores reusable results so repeated requests can avoid redundant computation. Cache invalidation and stale results must be handled carefully.
Continuous integration runs automated checks when code changes. A quality gate can fail a build when tests fail or a measured metric falls below an agreed threshold.
An ablation study removes or changes one component at a time to estimate its contribution to overall system performance.
An unanswerable question cannot be supported by the available knowledge base. A reliable retrieval-augmented system should recognize insufficient evidence instead of inventing an answer.
